Taejo entered the Hubaekje capital, ordered that the people not be touched, and thus united the three Han.

OLAYLAR_ORTACAG_DOGU_GUNEYDOGU_ASYA:1185.d: After Yoshitsune's opposition to Yoritomo, at the end of December 1185 the court, on Hojo Tokimasa's petition, granted Kamakura the authority to appoint and dismiss shugo (military-police governors) and jito (land/tax stewards) in every province. This is regarded as the moment when the bakufu gained permanent administrative authority in the provinces (Bunji kuni-jito).

OLAYLAR_ORTACAG_YER_SONRASI:1135-01-01:0.d: In the campaign of 1135 (and 1136-37), the Pisans, coming to the aid of Robert, Prince of Capua, at Naples against Roger II, King of Sicily, destroyed Amalfi and plundered the island of Ischia.

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_MISIR_NUBYA:-0321-01-01:0.d: Intervening in the strife at Cyrene, Ptolemy attached the Libyan region of Cyrenaica to Egypt under Ophellas. Thus Ptolemaic Egypt also expanded to the west; Cyrenaica remained in the hands of a branch of the Ptolemaic dynasty in the following centuries.

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_MISIR_NUBYA:-0330-01-01:0.d: Alexander crossed from the coast into the desert and went to the Siwa Oasis, where the Temple of Ammon stands, and consulted the oracle; Arrian writes that he received the answer that would please him. This visit fed Alexander's legitimacy in Egypt and the later accounts of his being regarded as the son of the god.

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_MISIR_NUBYA:-0359-01-01:0.b: Teos set out on a Syrian campaign; Nectanebo II seized the throne in a coup, and Agesilaus changed sides

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_MISIR_NUBYA:-2054-01-01:0.d: Mentuhotep II's long reign (51 years) is regarded as the beginning of the Middle Kingdom. In the first half of his reign Thebes was at war with Herakleopolis; in his 14th year, when Herakleopolitan forces violated the sacred cemetery at Abydos, the king sent an army north. The actual unification of Egypt came much later, around the 39th year of his reign (the entry below).

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_MISIR_NUBYA:0175-01-01:0.d: Cassius, commander of the eastern provinces, proclaimed himself emperor on the news of Marcus Aurelius's death; the revolt spread to Syria and Egypt (Dio records that the prefect of Egypt, Flavius Calvisius, because of his connection with the revolt, was not put to death afterward but exiled to an island). According to Dio, after a 'dream of empire' lasting three months and six days, Cassius was killed by one of his own officers; Marcus Aurelius visited Egypt and Syria and punished no one.

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_YAKIN_DOGU:-0329-01-01:0.d: Alexander, who passed the Persian Gates after Susa, reached Persepolis at the end of January 330; the city surrendered without resistance. Achaemenid rule at Persepolis ends this year (the palace was burned in May 330).

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_YAKIN_DOGU:-0732-01-01:0.d: When Pekah's Israel took a stand against Assyria together with Damascus, Tiglath-Pileser III turned northern Israel (Galilee, Gilead, the Megiddo region) into Assyrian provinces and carried out deportations; Hoshea replaced Pekah. The Kingdom of Israel was reduced to Samaria and the surrounding hill country.

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_YAKIN_DOGU:0363-06-26:0.b: Julian died near Samarra; the Sasanian war moved towards its end
OLAYLAR_ANTIK_YAKIN_DOGU:0363-06-26:0.d: After Julian's Ctesiphon campaign was halted by flooding, the Roman army retreated, and the emperor, wounded in a Sasanian attack at Maranga, died. Jovian, chosen by the army, was forced to make a treaty with Shapur II.

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_AKDENIZ:-0035-01-01:0.d: While reorganizing the East, Antony gave the throne of Cappadocia to Archelaus; Archelaus ruled until he was summoned to Rome by Tiberius in AD 17. Cappadocia became a Roman province in AD 17.

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_AKDENIZ:-0145-01-01:0.d: The Achaean League, which rebelled against Rome over a border dispute with Sparta, was defeated at Leucopetra in 146; Corinth was destroyed and the League was effectively dissolved, and part of Greece came under the supervision of the province of Macedonia.

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_AKDENIZ:-0166-01-01:1.b: Epirus plundered by Rome: seventy towns destroyed

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_AKDENIZ:-0263-01-01:1.d: When the Mamertines of Messana, after Carthage, also asked Rome for help against Hieron, king of Syracuse, the Roman consul Appius Claudius Caudex crossed to Sicily in 264 and took Messana from the Carthaginian garrison. Rome thus entered a war outside Italy for the first time.

OLAYLAR_ANTIK_AKDENIZ:-0310-01-01:0.b: Peace of the Diadochi: the rule of Antigonus over Asia, of Cassander over Europe and of Ptolemy over Egypt was recognized

OLAYLAR_ORTACAG_BEKLEYEN_ACIK:1207-01-01.d: The people of Corfu, who had resisted the attack of the Venetian fleet in 1205, surrendered only in 1207; the island was governed in the name of the Republic by a decarchy (a rule of ten men) of Venetian nobles.

OLAYLAR_ORTACAG_BEKLEYEN_ACIK:1247-01-01.d: The viscounty of Carcassonne (together with Béziers) was confiscated by the king in 1247 on account of the role played by Viscount Raymond Roger against Simon de Montfort in the Albigensian Crusade.

OLAYLAR_2S1019:1439-08-27:0.d: Smederevo was taken after a three-month siege. Hisarcık (Grocka), 17 km from Smederevo, follows on the map the fate of Smederevo, the center to which it was attached, and passes from the Serbian Despotate to the Ottomans on the same day (it will be returned in 1444).

OLAYLAR_2S1019:1458-08-06:0.d: In the Morea campaign, the Conqueror took Gördüs (Corinth) peacefully after a three-month siege. Sicyon, 17 km from Corinth, follows on the map the fate of Gördüs, the center to which it was attached, and passes to the Ottomans on the same day.

OLAYLAR_2S1019:1459-06-20:0.d: Helena, widow of Lazar Branković, surrendered the fortress of Smederevo to the Ottomans; the Serbian Despotate came to an end. Hisarcık (Grocka), attached to Smederevo, passes to the Ottomans on the same day.

OLAYLAR_2S1019:1475-06-06:0.d: After a four-day siege Caffa surrendered to Ahmed Pasha, and Mengli Giray accepted the vassalage of the Ottoman sultan. The area around Sochi, Tuapse and Maykop, homeland of the Circassian tribes who recognized the Crimean khans as suzerains, is shown on the map from this date as attached to the Crimean Khanate as a loose protectorate.

OLAYLAR_ALM1115B:1815-01-01:0.d: Friedrich Franz I, Duke of Mecklenburg-Schwerin, took the title of grand duchy ('großherzogliche Würde') in 1815; the entry for the Duchy of Mecklenburg (1348-1815) ends at this point, and the country continues as a grand duchy within the German Confederation.

OLAYLAR_LAB19_2S_P1:0613-05-12:0.d: Cobá Stela 6 opens with the Initial Series date 9.9.0.0.0, 3 Ajaw 2 Sotz'; in Gronemeyer's sequence it is attributed to Ruler A. The date of this inscription has been taken as the beginning of the Kingdom of Cobá.

OLAYLAR_LAB19_2S_P1:0780-12-02:0.d: Cobá Stela 20 opens with the Initial Series date 9.17.10.0.0, 12 Ajaw 8 Pax; it is the best-preserved monument at Cobá and is thought to describe a k'atun-ending celebration. The date of this inscription has been taken as the end of the Kingdom of Cobá ( the collapse of the kingdom is not described in this source).

OLAYLAR_LAB19_2S_P6:1944-10-20:0.b: Belgrade liberated by the Yugoslav People's Liberation Army and the Red Army

OLAYLAR_LAB19_BOS_1119_SIBIRYA:1630-01-0.b: Kirensk ostrog was founded: a Russian Cossack ostrog to subject the Tungus to tribute (yasak)

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_A_1029:0822-01-01:0.b: Last mention of the Avar Khaganate: the Hungarian plain no longer had a single owner (blank on the map afterwards)
OLAYLAR_AVMAC_A_1029:0822-01-01:0.d: The last political mention of the Avar state is around 822 (Pohl; Curta); afterwards the spheres of dominion of the Bulgars, the East Franks and Great Moravia competed, and no source naming a single owner for the area between the Danube and the Tisza could be found — the map shows this period as blank.

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_A_1029:1156-09-17:0.d: On 17 September 1156, at the Reichstag in Regensburg, Henry II Jasomirgott of Babenberg returned the duchy of Bavaria to the emperor, and the March of Austria was raised to a duchy entirely separate from Bavaria; Henry II had moved his residence from Klosterneuburg to Vienna around 1155.

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_A_1029:1180-01-01:0.d: The March of Styria, under the overlordship of the duke of Bavaria, became an independent duchy in 1180; Graz was the center of this duchy. The day is not in the source (the Diet of Gelnhausen is mentioned).

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_C_1029:1918-11-13:0.d: The proclamation written at Eckartsau is dated 13 November 1918; it was published in Budapest on 14 November. Charles renounced only the exercise of his sovereign rights and did not use the words 'abdication of the throne'. On the map Hungary changes on 11 November, while the People's Republic is proclaimed on 16 November; 13 November is the legal link between these two days.

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_C_1029:1918-11-16:0.d: Károlyi had been appointed prime minister by Charles on 31 October 1918 (Aster Revolution). On 16 November 1918 the National Council and government proclaimed the People's Republic; on 11 January 1919 Károlyi became provisional president. Hungary (After 1918: Republic → Regency) and the Hungarian People's Republic (Károlyi) begin from this day. With this event the cities of the Kingdom of Hungary outside Croatia, including Aquincum-Óbuda-Pest, Esztergom, Eger, Szeged, Debrecen, Oradea and Upper Hungary, passed to the Hungarian People's Republic.

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_C_1029:1919-03-21:0.d: When the Entente's Vix note (20 March) demanded the withdrawal of Hungarian troops, the Károlyi government withdrew; the communists, merged with the Social Democrats, founded the Soviet Republic on 21 March 1919. The Republic lasted 133 days (there is also a statement in TDV saying 121 days); the map shows this period under the entry Hungary (After 1918: Republic → Regency).

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_C_1029:1921-12-14:0.d: On 14-15 December 1921 Sopron and Brennbergbánya, and on 16 December the eight surrounding villages, voted. Hungary led in the city and Austria in most of the villages; in total Hungary received about 65 per cent. The Allied Generals' Commission handed the region over to Hungary on 1 January 1922 (on the map Sopron remains Hungarian).

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_C_1029:1945-07-09:0.d: The agreement on the occupation zones (Besatzungszonen) and the administration of the city of Vienna is dated 9 July 1945; the US, British and French forces arrived in their sectors on 1 September 1945, and the Allied Council met on 11 September. Four-power control lasted until 1955. The occupation zones are not shown separately on the map.

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_C_1029:1949-08-20:0.d: The constitution dated 20 August 1949 made Hungary a People's Republic. Here these two regimes are shown as a single state for 1946-1989; the map color does not change.

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_C_1029:1956-10-23:0.d: Excessive repression led to a popular uprising on 23 October 1956; Soviet troops intervened on 4 November. Territory and borders did not change; the regime continued under Kádár (Hungary (Second Republic 1946 → People's Republic 1949-08-20)).

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_C_1029:1995-01-01:0.d: Austria became an EU member on 1 January 1995, together with Sweden and Finland. The state and its borders did not change; on the map it continues as the Republic of Austria (Second Republic).

OLAYLAR_AVMAC_FINAL_1029:1703-01-01:0.d: Rákóczi's Brezán proclamation (cited as 6 May 1703) and Tamás Esze's meeting with the Kuruc troops in June 1703 began the uprising; the war ended with the Peace of Szatmár in 1711. Only the year is known: the day of the proclamation/beginning differs in secondary sources as 6 May, 21 May, 15 June; no academic source for the day was found.

OLAYLAR_AVUSTURYA_MACAR_1027:1523-01-01:.d: Half of Bregenz was sold to Duke Sigmund in 1451 and the remaining half to Archduke Ferdinand I in 1523; the map shows the change to full sovereignty in 1523, 1451-1523 being a period of half-sovereignty (no day was found).

OLAYLAR_FRANSA_KONTROL_1027:1481-12-11:3.d: Toulon, the port of Provence, became French with the passage of the county to the French crown (11 December 1481); there is no separate source specific to Toulon, the center to which it was attached, Aix-en-Provence, was taken as the basis (approximate information).

OLAYLAR_FRANSA_KONTROL_1027:1388-09-28:0.d: During the succession dispute among the Angevin heirs of Provence, Nice and its surroundings (the County of Nice) came under the dominion of Count Amadeus VII of Savoy on 28 September 1388; Nice remained in the Savoy/Sardinian dynasty until 1860 (apart from French occupations).

OLAYLAR_FRANSA_KONTROL_1027:1552-01-01:0.d: Toul, ruled by prince-bishops and dependent on the German Empire, was joined to France in 1552 (the Three Bishoprics together with Metz and Verdun); it was legally confirmed at Westphalia in 1648. The day of Metz (18 April 1552) is separate; for Toul there is no day in the source.

OLAYLAR_FRANSA_KONTROL_1027:1317-01-09:0.d: Louis X died on 5 July 1316; the regent Philip V proclaimed himself king after the posthumous son John I, who died 4 days after his birth, and was crowned at Reims on 9 January 1317. The day of the proclamation is not in the source; here the day of the coronation has been taken as the basis.

OLAYLAR_FRANSA_KONTROL_1027:1284-01-01:0.d: Through the marriage (1284) of Joan I, countess of Champagne and queen of Navarre, to Philip (IV), heir to France, Troyes, the capital of Champagne, was joined to the crown lands; for Meaux, Treccani says in the same year (1284) 'it passed to the king of France'. The official annexation of the county is in 1314 with the accession of Louis X.

OLAYLAR_FRANSA_KONTROL_1027:1360-10-24:0.d: The preliminary agreement of Brétigny of 8 May 1360 was ratified at Calais on 24 October 1360: Poitou, Saintonge, Aunis, Agenais, Périgord, Limousin, Quercy, Angoumois and Rouergue were left to England. Limoges, La Rochelle and Poitiers pass to England on the map on this day.

OLAYLAR_FRANSA_KONTROL_1027:1420-05-21:0.d: The treaty signed at Troyes on 21 May 1420 between Charles VI and Henry V, King of England, made Henry V regent of France and heir to the throne; the Dauphin Charles (Charles VII) was excluded from the inheritance. The treaty transfers no territory; Champagne (Troyes, Reims) remained from this date until 1429 under English-Burgundian ('Lancastrian France') administration, and the map shows this administration as England.

OLAYLAR_FRANSA_KONTROL_1027:1420-05-21:1.d: The treaty signed at Troyes on 21 May 1420 between Charles VI and Henry V, King of England, made Henry V regent of France and heir to the throne; the Dauphin Charles (Charles VII) was excluded from the inheritance. The treaty transfers no territory; Champagne (Troyes, Reims) remained from this date until 1429 under English-Burgundian ('Lancastrian France') administration, and the map shows this administration as England.

OLAYLAR_NAPOLYON_ITALYA_1028:1800-06-04:.d: After the victory of Marengo, Napoleon returned to Milan and re-established the Cisalpine Republic (the date of 2 June is also given for this event).

OLAYLAR_NAPOLYON_ITALYA_1028:1143-01-01:.d: The people of Rome re-established the commune and the senate on the Capitol; under the influence of Arnold of Brescia, papal sovereignty was in effect not recognized until 1155 (1143 has been taken as the basis for the beginning; Treccani gives 1144).

OLAYLAR_NAPOLYON_ITALYA_1028:1128-01-01:.d: In 1128 Roger II took the duchy of Apulia and Bohemond II's principality of Taranto/Otranto/Brindisi (May-June 1128; according to a secondary source). On the map this change is shown on the same day as Bari and Salerno.

OLAYLAR_NAPOLYON_ITALYA_1028:1128-01-01:.b: Lecce passed from the Duchy of Apulia to the Kingdom of Sicily (Roger II; the date has been taken as the same as Bari's)

OLAYLAR_NAPOLYON_ITALYA_1028:1128-01-01:.d: Calabria became part of the Kingdom of Sicily with the passing of the duchy of Apulia and Calabria to Roger II (1128); no dated sentence specific to the city was found; the date of Bari and Melfi has been taken as the basis.

OLAYLAR_OK104:1284-01-01:0.d: Durrës and Krujë, which Charles of Anjou had taken in 1271-1272, were retaken after Charles's death by the Byzantine emperor Andronikos II (TDV Kruya: 'he retook Valona, Durrës and Krujë'). Only the year is known.

OLAYLAR_OK104:1344-01-01:0.d: TDV Kruya: 'in 1344 the Serbs captured Krujë, Berat and Vlorë'. TDV Arnavutluk says that Dušan occupied Albania between 1343 and 1346, and that with the collapse of his empire in 1355 the local lords grew stronger. Only the year is known.

OLAYLAR_OK104:1443-01-01:0.d: After the defeat at Zlatitsa (İzladi) (TDV Kruya: 847/1443), Skanderbeg occupied Krujë. After the death of his father Gjon Kastrioti in 1437, the Ottomans had given the city not to him but to Hasan Bey, whom they appointed. Only the year is known; the day could not be verified.

OLAYLAR_OK104:1304-01-01:0.d: In Durrës, which had passed to Byzantium in 1284, Philip, Prince of Taranto, son of King Charles II of Naples, re-established Angevin rule in 1304; the Kingdom of Albania (Regnum Albaniae) was proclaimed anew, but in Philip's lifetime it remained limited to this city (Europange: 'The kingdom of Albania was re-established in 1304, when Philip of Taranto was able to restore the Angevin regime in Durazzo'). In 1332 his son Robert gave Durrës to John of Gravina in exchange for the Principality of Achaea; the duchy of Durazzo remained in Angevin hands until Charles Thopia took the city in 1368. Only the year is known.

OLAYLAR_P0917KOSU13:1731-11-15:0.d: Hekimoğlu Ali Pasha retook Tabriz, which had fallen into Safavid hands in 1730, on 15 November 1731; Urmia was taken in the same operation. But by the treaty of 10 January 1732 Tabriz was left to Iran. The map also shows Kotur, which is considered to have shared the same fate as Hoy, as having passed from the Safavids to the Ottomans on this day (TDV Hoy; no day specific to Kotur in the source — approximate information).

OLAYLAR_P0068:1789-10-13:0.d: In the third year of the war the Austrian commander Loudon took the Ottoman frontier fortresses along the Danube. Smederevo surrendered on 13 October 1789 on condition that the garrison's 300 soldiers leave after laying down their arms; Belgrade, which had been an Ottoman frontier fortress for fifty years, also passed into Austrian hands the same autumn. Between 1789 and 1791 Loudon had entrenchments built commanding the citadel and suburb of Smederevo. Both cities were returned to the Ottoman State by the Treaty of Sistova signed on 4 August 1791; for this reason both are shown on the map as occupation, not annexation. The day of Belgrade's surrender does not appear in any of the four TDV entries examined (the entry gives only the year); the date here is the day of Smederevo, and for Belgrade it is not an estimate but the only known day of the same operation.

OLAYLAR_P0067:1788-09-21:0.d: The Ottoman forces under the command of Kethüdâ Hasan Pasha, the serasker of Vidin, defeated Joseph II's army at Caransebeș also, after Mehadia. In a council in the tent of the grand vizier-commander it was decided to attack the enemy camp; while preparations continued during the night, the Austrian troops were seen to have abandoned their positions and withdrawn to the town of Caransebeș. The pursuing Ottoman forces pinned them down in the town; in the fire that broke out many soldiers were killed, the survivors took refuge at Lugoj, seven hours away, and more than a thousand people were taken prisoner. The Austrian army's own campaign diary records the same night as a panic and friendly fire. The city did not come into Ottoman possession: it was taken, burned and abandoned on 10 October 1788 — for this reason no change of frontier appears on the map.

OLAYLAR_P0068B:1789-09-22:0.d: The Ottoman army suffered a heavy rout on 22 September 1789 while crossing the Rymnik river and then on the bank of the Boza water. This second defeat, coming seven weeks after Focșani, in effect broke up the Wallachian front and led to the surrender of the fortresses on the Dniester line in October-November: the TDV entry on Koca Yûsuf Pasha gives the surrender of Izmail on 11 October and of Bender on 14 November. However, the surrender of Izmail in 1789 does not occur in the TDV entry İsmâil (the fortress is still in Ottoman hands in 1790), and ESBE also writes that after Rymnik only Hacıbey and Akkerman were taken and that Bender surrendered on 3 November (Julian; = 14 November); the TDV entry on Akkirman also records that the fortress was taken by the Russians in 1789. The surrender of 11 October is most probably that of Akkerman — since the day could not be confirmed for Akkerman in the source read, it is not shown separately on the map.

OLAYLAR_DUNYA_BOLGE_1109:1917-03-15:0.d: Nicholas II declared that he abdicated on behalf of himself and his son; with his brother Mikhail's refusal to accept the crown the next day, the Romanov dynasty, which had lasted 304 years since 1613, and the three-century autocratic monarchy officially ended. In Russian historiography, it is on the same level as Kulikovo, 1613, 1812 and 1861 the closing date of the imperial period.

OLAYLAR_GEZGINLER:1522-09-06:0.d: The Victoria entered Sanlúcar on 6 September 1522 and anchored at Seville on 8 September; of the 5 ships that set out, only one returned, with about 18 men (the number of men is based on general knowledge).
